lessons.title: Greeting at a lunch counter
lessons.objective: Greet staff politely at lunch, say your name, and recognize common lunch words in kana.
lessons.focus: こんにちは is a daytime greeting. すみません gets a server’s attention politely. は is pronounced wa in わたしは; です closes a polite statement. Katakana marks loanwords such as メニュー and ジュース.

lessons.title: Numbers, yen, and portions

lessons.title: Describing food and finding a seat
lessons.objective: Ask whether a seat is available, describe food temperature and taste, and say where a place is.
lessons.focus: Japanese does not use a ser/estar split. おいしい and 辛い describe qualities; 熱い describes hot food. 空いています says a seat is available, and 近くです says a place is nearby.

lessons.title: Going to lunch and paying by card

lessons.title: What I do not eat
